co_dakota_hogback_submitted_as_bear_cany.blurb: A small sandstone fin on the eastern edge of Bear Creek Cañon Park, west of Colorado Springs. The formation holds about 18 routes, a mix of sport lines and gear climbs, and most are easy to moderate: mainly 5.6 to 5.9, with a single 5.11. The gear routes face the west side, while boulder problems sit on the opposite side. The stone is soft, porous and gravelly in spots, so quality varies, and it deserves a few dry days after rain or snow. The base is only a short uphill walk from the trail, which suits newer leaders and a quick visit.

co_parachute_rock.blurb: Parachute Rock is a pinnacle in the South Platte country along Rampart Range Road, at roughly 9,300 feet. It is mainly a gear-climbing venue, with a lone sport line and a single aid route, and the grades run from 5.6 up to 5.11, with the bulk of them between 5.8 and 5.10. Expect cracks, slabs and a wide offwidth on climbs of one or two pitches. Summit routes finish with an easy walk down, and the trail from the roadside pullout to the base takes only five to ten minutes. The top gives views toward Pikes Peak.

co_sob_gully_skier_s_left_side.blurb: A set of long gear routes on the north rim of the Black Canyon of the Gunnison, on the skier's-left side of the gully that serves as the usual way into the canyon. All 18 climbs are trad, ranging from 5.8 to 5.12 with the heaviest concentration at 5.10 and 5.11, and many stretch to seven or eight pitches. The north rim style is committing: demanding route finding, some runouts, and little chance of quick help in an emergency. The gully entrance is signed and just off the road, and the hike down is quick, though poison ivy grows along it.

co_twilight_wall.blurb: Twilight Wall is the largest cliff in the Twilight Area, in the Narrows of Poudre Canyon near Fort Collins. The face carries medium-length sport routes on well-featured, good-quality rock, plus a couple of hard boulder problems at its base. Sport grades run from 5.10 to 5.13, but most sit between 5.11 and 5.12, so this is a place for stronger climbers rather than beginners. The wall catches sun in the morning. Reaching it means getting across the river, and water level largely decides when you can go, which favors fall through spring.
